item.title: Go Daily Question 20250530
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import "sync"

func main() {
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	foo := make(chan int)
	bar := make(chan int)
	wg.Add(1)
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		select {
		case foo <- <-bar:
		default:
			println("default")
		}
	}()
	wg.Wait()
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Correct Answer: Deadlock (no output, program hangs)

Analysis:

This code will deadlock; it will not output “default” nor panic. Instead, the program will hang and cannot continue execution. The reasons are as follows:

item.title: Go Daily Question 20250527
item.description:
Process of sending and receiving data on a channel

🔑 Answer Analysis:
  • Sending data
    • Uninitialized channels will deadlock.
    • Closed channels will panic.
    • If a blocked Goroutine is waiting to read, data is written and the reader is unblocked.
    • If no blocked reader exists, and the channel is buffered, it checks for available space. If space exists, data is written to the buffer.
    • If the buffer is full, the sender blocks.
  • Receiving data
    • Uninitialized channels will deadlock.
    • Closed channels will return the zero value.
    • Unbuffered:
      • If a blocked Goroutine is waiting to write, data is read and the writer is unblocked.
    • Buffered: checks if there’s available space. If no content, the receiver Goroutine blocks and is added to the read queue. If content exists, data is read from the buffer.

item.title: Go Daily Question 207
item.description:
What happens when the following code is executed?

package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "time"
)

func main() {
    ch := make(chan int, 1000)
    go func() {
        for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
            ch <- i
        }
    }()
    go func() {
        for {
            a, ok := <-ch
            if !ok {
                fmt.Println("close")
                return
            }
            fmt.Println("a: ", a)
        }
    }()
    close(ch)
    fmt.Println("ok")
    time.Sleep(time.Second * 100)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
ok
close
panic: send on closed channel

goroutine 6 [running]:

Writing data to a closed channel will cause a panic. Reading data from a closed channel, when there’s no buffered data, will read the zero value.

item.title: Go Daily Question 150
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (
       "fmt"
       "time"
)

func main() {
       ch1 := make(chan int)
       go fmt.Println(<-ch1)
       ch1 <- 5
       time.Sleep(1 * time.Second)
}
  • A: 5
  • B: Cannot compile
  • C: Runtime deadlock
🔑 Answer Analysis:

C Run online

fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!

Official description of Go statements

A go statement starts a new goroutine (concurrent thread of execution) and executes a function call in that goroutine.

item.title: Go Daily Question 131
item.description:
Regarding channels, which of the following syntax is correct:

  • A. var ch chan int
  • B. ch := make(chan int)
  • C. <- ch
  • D. ch <-
🔑 Answer Analysis:

A, B, C

A declares variable ch of type chan int, but does not initialize it. B declares variable ch of type chan int, and initializes it. C reads from the channel, discarding the value. D is incorrect; writing to a channel requires a value.

item.title: Go Daily Question 095
item.description:
Output of the following code:

package main

import "sync"

func main() {
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    foo := make(chan int)
    bar := make(chan int)
    wg.Add(1)
    go func() {
        defer wg.Done()
        select {
        case foo <- <-bar:
        default:
            println("default")
        }
    }()
    wg.Wait()
}

A: default B: panic

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Conventionally, one might expect the default branch of the select statement in go func to execute, and the program to run normally. However, the result is not that, but a deadlock. You can test this via: https://play.studygolang.com/p/kF4pOjYXbXf.

item.description:
Regarding channels, which of the following syntax is correct:

A. var ch chan int
B. ch := make(chan int)
C. <- ch
D. ch <-
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: ABC

A and B both declare a channel; C reads from a channel; Writing to a channel must include a value, so D is incorrect.

item.title: Go Daily Question 037
item.description:
What happens when the following code is executed?

package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "time"
)

func main() {
    ch := make(chan int, 1000)
    go func() {
        for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
            ch <- i
        }
    }()
    go func() {
        for {
            a, ok := <-ch
            if !ok {
                fmt.Println("close")
                return
            }
            fmt.Println("a: ", a)
        }
    }()
    close(ch)
    fmt.Println("ok")
    time.Sleep(time.Second * 100)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: Prints “ok” then panics. It takes time to start goroutines. Here, the close(ch) statement closes the channel. Writing data to an already closed channel will cause a program panic.
